correctness.rationale: Poisson superposition gives exact correspondence of the stopped coupon process and maximum of iid exponential first arrivals. Conditioning on the maximum yields 1+Bin(n-1,ye^{-y}/(1-e^{-y})), with mean~log(n)e^{-x} and variance~log(n)e^{-x} uniformly for bounded x. Conditional characteristic functions give joint Gumbel/mixed-Gaussian convergence. Conditional moments of zero-truncated Poisson counts imply T_n/n-M_n=O_P(sqrt(log n/n)), and the proposed random centers differ by o_P(sqrt(log n)). Integration over E~Exp(1) proves the Gamma joint transform and Laplace marginal. Finite exact and numerical tests: 724 successful assertions; no finite test used as an infinite proof.

value.rationale: The theorem gives a natural second-order law of singleton uncertainty after observing full collection time: conditionally Gaussian noise with a random exponential variance becomes non-Gaussian Laplace unconditionally. It characterizes a genuinely random stopping-boundary effect with an exact joint Gumbel characteristic transform, not merely the harmonic mean, the established first-order exponential limit or a recomputed finite table.
